keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Kerman Seljuk row). Qavurt 'defeated the Buyid ruler's army in Kerman and Makran in around 1041' (Qavurt page); infobox territory 'Kerman', Makran linked to the early conquests. The page gives no area. Oman (suzerainty 1053-1154) and the emir of Hormuz (submitted, undated) are not drawn as territory; Oman is a vassal tint in the ledger. Fars was invaded in 1053 or 1062 and Shiraz 'handed over' in 1062 but no tenure is given, so it is not drawn.

New keyframe. By 1186 Muhammad-Shah 'had been unable to handle the Ghuzz' and left Bam and Kerman; Malik Dinar seized Kerman. Only the exile seat at Bam remains until the 1187 disestablishment (infobox).

ledger.note: 1041: Qavurt founds the Kerman Seljuk sultanate. He 'defeated the Buyid ruler's army in Kerman and Makran in around 1041' and laid 'the foundations of his own new sultanate in around 1048' (Qavurt page); infobox 'Established: 1041 (429 AH)'. He ruled as a subject of Tughril I, de facto independent.

region.text: Oman, under Seljuk suzerainty after Qavurt deposed the Buyid governor

ledger.note: 1053: Oman comes under the Kerman Seljuks. The page says the territory 'also included Oman' between 1053 and 1154; the Qavurt page: Qavurt deposed the Buyid governor and 'brought Oman under Seljuk suzerainty', undated but before Malik Shah's accession in 1072.

region.text: Oman, under Seljuk suzerainty after Qavurt deposed the Buyid governor

ledger.note: 1154: Oman leaves the Kerman Seljuks (the page's 1053-1154 span); the nabhani-dynasty dossier begins in 1154.

region.text: Kerman province: Kerman, Bardasir (Bardsir), Bam, Jiroft

ledger.note: 1186: the Ghuzz take Kerman. Muhammad-Shah, 'unable to handle the Ghuzz', left Bam and Kerman; 'Malik Dinar seized Kerman'. Infobox: Bam capital-in-exile 1186-1187.

1187: the sultanate is disestablished (infobox: 1187, 583 AH). The page says Kerman was annexed by the Khwarazmians only in 1196 and Muhammad-Shah served the Ghurids; Bam's fate after 1187 is not on the page.

wars.name: Battle of Kerj Abu Dulaf
wars.outcome: Malik Shah defeated Qavurt's forces near Hamadan on 16 May 1073; Qavurt was arrested and executed. Kerman stayed a (vassal) sultanate under Kerman Shah and Sultan Shah (the great-seljuk-empire dossier carries the 1074 vassalage).

wars.name: Qavurt's rebellions against Alp Arslan
wars.outcome: Qavurt begged forgiveness in December 1064, rebelled in 1067 minting coins in his own name, was pardoned and kept as governor of Kerman, and rebelled again c. 1068-69, giving up after failing to win the campaign (Qavurt page). No border change.

wars.name: Qavurt's invasion of Fars
wars.outcome: The Qavurt page dates the invasion of Fars to 1053 in one reference and 1062 in another; in 1062 Shiraz was handed over to him. No later tenure is given, so Fars is not drawn.

wars.name: Ghuzz conquest of Kerman

zones.text: Kerman province: Kerman, Bardasir (Bardsir), Bam, Jiroft

wars.outcome: Malik Dinar seized Kerman in 1186 and Muhammad-Shah withdrew to Bam; the Khwarazmians annexed Kerman in 1196.

certainty.note: Kerman province is the stable core; the Makran and Oman limits, the Hormuz coast and the Fars frontier are not defined on the pages opened. The sultans' autonomy under Tughril I, Alp Arslan and Malik Shah is a status question, not a frontier.

notes:
A state Cliopatria lacks (cliopatria_names []). Two pages used (the Kerman Seljuk Sultanate page is thin and gives no area); the Qavurd title did not exist and the 'Malik Dinar' title is a different man. Wikidata id not obtainable: null.
Not settled: the Ghuzz of Kerman 1186-1196 (Malik Dinar) are not a Cliopatria or dossier state; a further page on them and on the Qutlugh-Khanids (1223 onward) should be opened by a gap-filler. Emir Badr Isa of Hormuz submitted to Qavurt (undated, Qavurt page): the Hormuz coast is not drawn; the Kingdom of Hormuz dossier (if written) should record it. Fars: Qavurt invaded in 1053 or 1062 and Shiraz was handed over in 1062, with no end of tenure on any page, so it is not drawn. Qavurt's 1048 Bardasir surrender is inside Kerman.
The vassalage of the Kerman Seljuks to the Great Seljuks (the great-seljuk-empire dossier has vassal_start 1074 and vassal_end 1187 under 'kerman-seljuk-sultanate') is the suzerain's event; the Kerman page itself calls Qavurt a subject of Tughril I from 1041 (a coin of 1056/7 names Chaghri Beg as overlord). Oman 1053-1154 is the page's span for inclusion; whether it was suzerainty or direct rule is not settled.
